public_rationale: In November 2024 OpenAI's own researchers wrote that current frontier models still produce false outputs, known as hallucinations, and called factual accuracy an open problem (e1). On their new SimpleQA benchmark, GPT-4o and Claude both scored under 50% on short fact questions (e2). No cited source shows a method that reliably removed hallucinations across tasks by the end of 2024. The plain reading of 'no robust solution' therefore holds.
limitations: The main source is a lab paper, though it describes the lab's own limits.
Grounded settings such as retrieval or summarization show lower rates, but not zero.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is still no robust solution to LLM hallucinations.

statement.excerpt: There is still no robust solution to hallucinations.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the end of 2024, no available method reliably stopped LLMs from producing confident false statements across ordinary tasks.
He states a current condition without a period. Since the post reviews 2024, the target period is calendar 2024 up to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from late 2024 shows leading LLMs still hallucinate at meaningful rates, or that leading labs still treat hallucination as unsolved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence shows a method or model that, by the end of 2024, reliably removed hallucinations across varied tasks in independent tests.
